newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-HENDERSON EQUALS COURSE RECORD, LENDL STARTS WELL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HENDERSON EQUALS COURSE RECORD, LENDL STARTS WELL.

text.p: Scott Henderson equalled the Karlstein course record with a seven-under-par 64 to take an early one-stroke lead from fellow-Briton Simon Hurley in the Czech Open on Thursday.
Henderson, a 27-year-old Scot, fashioned his lead on an opening eagle when he holed a seven foot putt on the par five first, three putted the second, then followed up with six birdies .
Hurley, who has come back after six weeks out with an injured wrist, also included an eagle with six birdies, but dropped two shots.

Former tennis world number one Ivan Lendl made a remarkable start to his second Czech Open as a golf professional when he began his round with three threes -- birdie, birdie, par -- to be two under after three holes.
Fair play award winner Michael Long of New Zealand, aiming for a top 10 finish, came in with a group two strokes behind the lead.

Long won the award after he forfeited the chance of a playoff with Johnnie Walker Classic winner Ernie Els in Australia at the European Tour's first event of the season when he called a one-stroke penalty on himself with a hole to go in the final round at the Gold Coast.
"I'm looking for a top-10 here," said Long after carding 66, "so that I will be given an exemption to the European Open in Ireland the week after next.
"Of course top-one would do nicely, but I'd take top 10 to give me an extra event so that I can continue getting good experience of European Tour courses for next year when I can play all year.
